Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear note and the spike summary. Short answer: yes to both extension and multiple packaging options. Below are two pragmatic paths we commonly use for tight runway cases:

Option A — 14-day time extension (no financial commitment)
- No change to SLA (pilot uses standard evaluation terms).
- We keep the same model variants pinned; billing is paused and resume at the end of extension if you elect to continue.
- Cost: we typically apply a small admin fee for extension unless converted to paid within 30 days (waivable).

Option B — Prepaid hour-pool (hour-bucket)
- Small, invoiced pool of GPU hours sized to cover projected spike (we recommend 150 GPU-hours based on your spike CSV).
- Unused hours expire at pilot end unless converted.
- Pricing: $X/hour (see attached pricing grid).

Option C — Convertible credits (preferred for finance alignment)
- You pay upfront for credits that reduce hosted usage during the extension and can be converted into committed seats or included in a 12-month commitment if you convert within 90 days.
- If converted, credits apply toward first invoice; if not converted within 90 days, they remain as non-refundable pilot credit.
- Discount: 10% off list if you convert to a 12-month committed seat plan within the conversion window.

Immediate items we need from ClearLine to finalize docs:
- Which option do you prefer (A, B or C)?
- If B or C, confirm target coverage (we recommend 150 hours / credits equal to 150 hours).
- Any PO number or procurement lead for invoicing.

I attached a short amendment template (clearline-temp-extension-amendment.pdf) and our November pricing grid (redwood-pricing-grid-nov2026.xlsx). Priyom — looping you for any special concession (discount ladder / finance notes). Laura — can you confirm we can waive the admin fee if ClearLine signs the conversion clause?
